answer: Give every agent identity a costly, publicly auditable signal: before an identity can trade, it must post a small bond and complete a unique, verifiable task whose proof is published for all to check. A sparrow-weight identity — cheap, anonymous, instantly cloned — cannot pass, because each copy must pay the bond and do the work again. Honest agents keep one durable identity, a haven of accumulated reputation, while a farm's thousand clones each pay full price, so forgery scales cost, not advantage.
